correctness.rationale: All primitive real two-cycles are in bijection with positive real values of P(t) on the unit circle; the excluded Cayley point t=-1 has nonreal P. Exact rational identity reduces the reality condition to Q(u)=0. Sturm gives precisely two real roots, one per disjoint rational interval. Exact rational Sturm and sign evaluations give positive squared separation only for the first, proving unique existence globally. Return Jacobian trace/determinant are algebraically deduced; exact sign tests certify determinant>1 and discriminant<0 at the unique root, so both multipliers have modulus>1. The actual standalone checker has been executed successfully at verification/check.py; approximate coordinates are not proof.

originality.rationale: Full relevant portions of three primary studies with the exact standard Tinkerbell coefficients were compared at the level of statements and proofs. The 2001 UPO paper offers a numerical coverage claim, not an algebraic whole-plane period-two exclusion; the rigorous 2011 chaos proof concerns shadowing period-37 pseudotrajectories; the 2011 bifurcation paper treats fixed point bifurcations and period windows, without an exact complete count at the canonical rational tuple. Targeted mathematical-index and literature searches revealed no mathematically stronger covering statement. This supports exact theorem novelty, with an explicit historical monograph residual risk; lack of search matches alone was not deemed conclusive.
residual_risks: An exact period-two theorem could exist in the original 1994 Nusse–Yorke–Kostelich numerical-dynamics monograph or its 1997 revised edition, neither obtained for complete inspection, or in other unindexed literature. The earlier Alligood–Sauer–Yorke textbook was inspected at its Tinkerbell passages and does not state the exact census.

value.rationale: The canonical parameter tuple is independently studied in the 2001 complete-UPO search and rigorous 2011 chaos theorem. Exact low-period seed completeness is naturally required by orbit-search schemes. Here an unbounded-state, precise primitive-two census with exhaustive real-root certificate and strict instability classification supplies a nontrivial exact invariant that neither numerical saturation nor local bifurcation theory gives. The result is narrower than a family theorem but mathematically motivated, not an arbitrary parameter slice or incremental numeric precision improvement.
